correctness.rationale: The nodal Gram matrix follows from exact edgewise integration. The displayed block inverse is independently verified by multiplication. At every vertex, the edgewise affine inverse-kernel coefficients give one sign change on each edge and an exact integral \(7/3-4w/[3(1+w)]\); all output extrema are vertices. Kernel symmetry gives the L1 norm. Positive normalized factors give \(\vartheta\le1/\max(a,b)\) with all equality configurations; the zero-factor limit gives nonattained supremum. The identity P1=1 gives the sharp negative excursion. Reconstructing independent rational Gram inverses on 144 weighted bipartite factor choices agreed exactly. No finite test is used as proof of the universal result.

value.rationale: The natural rank-one length model of a multiply connected graph yields a completely sharp stability and positivity-defect invariant for nodal L2 least-squares smoothing. The operator norm depends only on the smallest color-normalized length factor, not the individual ab edge lengths, which explains an exact and surprisingly nonunique optimizer set when the two color classes have unequal sizes. The sharp worst-input construction and max-to-min length design classification directly inform uniform approximation stability; this precise norm is not simply a restatement of matrix conditioning.
